channel.title: Audience on Best of AI
channel.description: Recent content in Audience on Best of AI

item.title: Discord
item.description:
Community managers set roles, channels, and rules, and use bots for moderation and welcome messages. Voice channels and events support live sessions. AutoMod features filter spam and harmful content.

Free to use, with optional paid subscriptions. It works best for real-time chat, and information can get buried.

Slack and Circle are alternatives. Discord suits community managers running active chat communities.

item.title: Mighty Networks
item.description:
Mighty Networks is a platform for building a membership community. A creator sets up a space with feeds, groups, live events, and online courses, and members join by paying a subscription or one-time fee. The pitch is an experience that feels like your own app, with mobile apps that can carry your brand.

Monetization is built in. Creators can charge for memberships, courses, and events, offer tiered access, and run bundles. The AI assistant helps with tasks such as naming a community, drafting posts and course outlines, and suggesting engagement ideas. Analytics show member activity, which helps community managers improve retention.

item.title: Skool
item.description:
Skool is a simple platform for running a community. Members post in a feed, take courses in a classroom section, attend events from a shared calendar, and earn points for participating, which unlock levels on a leaderboard. The gamification is meant to keep people engaged without a lot of setup.

The pricing and design are deliberately simple. Skool charges a flat fee for community owners and offers few customization options, so creators spend time on content and members, not on configuring a site. Communities can charge a monthly or annual fee, and a built-in discovery page, plus members’ direct messages, helps people find groups.

item.title: TubeBuddy
item.description:
TubeBuddy is a browser extension and mobile app for YouTube creators. It adds tools to the YouTube interface, including a keyword explorer that estimates how competitive a search term is, tag suggestions, and a score that shows how well a video is optimized. These help creators choose topics and fill in titles and descriptions with search in mind.

Other features save time. Bulk tools update many videos at once, thumbnail A/B testing compares designs for click rates, and scheduling and reminders organize publishing. Analytics show how a channel performs and how it compares to others. AI tools suggest titles, descriptions, and ideas based on a video’s topic.

item.title: Circle
item.description:
Circle gives communities a home of their own. A creator sets up spaces for topics, posts content, hosts live events, runs courses, and lets members message each other, all under a custom domain and brand. It aims to feel more focused than a social network and less cluttered than a forum.

Monetization is built in. Communities can charge for memberships, offer paid tiers, and sell courses and events, with workflows to onboard new members. AI features draft welcome messages, summarize conversations, and help members find information, while analytics show engagement and which members are most active. Mobile apps and integrations with tools like Zapier extend reach.

item.title: VidIQ
item.description:
vidIQ helps YouTubers grow. A browser extension adds data to YouTube pages and Studio, showing keyword scores, competitor stats, and tags used by successful videos. Research tools find topics with demand and low competition.

AI features suggest video ideas, titles, and thumbnails, write descriptions, and give feedback on videos. Analytics track subscriber growth and performance, and a coach feature gives guidance.

vidIQ has a free plan and paid tiers. Optimization scores are guides, and content quality drives results. Alternatives include TubeBuddy, Morningfame, Social Blade, and YouTube’s own research tools. vidIQ suits creators optimizing a channel.

item.title: Planable
item.description:
Planable is built around approval workflows. Marketers create posts in a view that looks like the final social post, share it with teammates or clients, collect comments and approvals, and schedule it once signed off. This replaces long email chains and screenshots.

Features include a content calendar, multiple approval stages, and support for many networks. AI tools help draft captions and ideas. Agencies find it useful for client work where sign-off is required.

item.title: Sprinklr
item.description:
Sprinklr serves very large organizations. It manages publishing across social channels, listens for brand mentions, handles customer care across messaging and voice, and analyzes market trends, using a shared data layer so teams see the whole customer picture.

AI runs through the platform: models classify conversations, detect sentiment, route cases, suggest replies, and generate content, and agents handle some customer interactions. Governance tools suit regulated industries and large teams.

Sprinklr is sold on enterprise subscriptions, with high cost and complexity. Alternatives include Hootsuite, Sprout Social, Khoros, Emplifi, and Salesforce. Sprinklr suits large brands managing many channels.

item.title: Buffer
item.description: Buffer is built for people who want to run their social accounts without living in each app. You connect your profiles, write a post once, adjust it per platform, and schedule it into a queue that publishes at set times. A calendar view shows what is planned, and an idea library keeps drafts and inspiration in one place. The interface is deliberately plain, which is a big part of why freelancers, creators, and small businesses like it.

item.title: ContentStudio
item.description:
ContentStudio combines content discovery, creation, and publishing. Users find trending topics and articles, curate and share them, write posts with an AI assistant, and schedule to networks such as Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, X, TikTok, and WordPress blogs. A calendar shows what is planned across channels.

Features for teams and agencies include approval workflows, client management, white-label reports, and analytics on performance. The AI writer generates captions, hashtags, and blog drafts, and image tools help create visuals. Social inbox features centralize replies and comments.

item.title: Flick AI
item.description:
Flick targets people who manage social media without a large team. It combines content planning with AI writing: you can brainstorm ideas, generate captions and post drafts in your own style, and organize them on a calendar before scheduling. A hashtag tool suggests relevant tags, and an analytics view helps you see what performs well.

An AI assistant trained on your past content tries to match your tone and topics, so drafts need less editing than generic output. The platform supports multiple networks, including Instagram, LinkedIn, and TikTok, and offers collaboration features for agencies or small teams to review and approve content. Prompts and templates help with common formats such as carousels and short videos.

item.title: Hootsuite
item.description:
Hootsuite is one of the oldest social media management tools. Teams connect accounts for networks such as Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, X, TikTok, and YouTube, plan content on a calendar, schedule posts, and respond to comments and messages in a shared inbox. Approval workflows suit larger organizations.

Listening and analytics tools track brand mentions and compare performance across channels. OwlyWriter, the AI assistant, helps write captions, suggest ideas, and repurpose content. Advertising management and employee advocacy products extend the suite for enterprises.

item.title: Later
item.description:
Later started as a way to plan Instagram feeds visually. Users drag photos and videos onto a calendar, see how the grid will look, write captions, and schedule posts to go out automatically. It has since expanded to other networks, including TikTok, Pinterest, LinkedIn, Facebook, and X, with tools to manage a content library, collaborate with teammates, and track results.

Other features support social growth. A link-in-bio page lets creators send followers to multiple destinations, analytics show which posts perform best and when audiences are most active, and AI helps write captions, suggest hashtags, and repurpose content. The company also owns an influencer marketing platform, which helps brands find creators and manage campaigns.

item.title: Metricool
item.description:
Metricool brings several marketing tasks into one dashboard. Users can plan and schedule posts across networks on a calendar, see analytics on posts, followers, and competitors, and manage Facebook, Instagram, Google, and TikTok ads reports. A link-in-bio tool, inbox for comments and messages, and web analytics help connect social activity to site traffic.

Reporting is a strong point. Customizable reports can be exported or scheduled for clients, and integrations connect with Looker Studio and other business intelligence tools, which suits agencies. AI features help write captions, suggest posting times, and generate content ideas, and a feature can plan a calendar from a brief. Plans cover multiple brands, so one account can manage several clients.

item.title: Missinglettr
item.description:
Missinglettr automates a task many content creators neglect: promoting their articles over time. You connect your blog or paste a link, and the tool analyzes the post to pull out quotes, statistics, and highlights. It then generates a series of social posts, with images, scheduled across weeks and months, so a single article continues to attract visitors long after it’s published.

Other features round out the platform. A curation tool suggests relevant content from other sources to share, a social media scheduler handles regular posting, and analytics show engagement. Collaboration features allow agencies and teams to manage several brands. AI helps with writing captions and variations, and automated hashtag suggestions save time.

item.title: SocialBee
item.description:
SocialBee organizes posting by category, such as promotions, tips, and behind-the-scenes, so a profile keeps a deliberate mix rather than random posts. Evergreen content can be recycled automatically, and a calendar shows what is scheduled.

AI helps generate posts, captions, and images, and its Copilot suggests a strategy and content plan from a business description. Team features support approvals and client work, and analytics report performance.

SocialBee is paid, with plans by profiles. Alternatives include Buffer, Later, Publer, Hootsuite, and Metricool. SocialBee suits small businesses and agencies.

item.title: Sprout Social
item.description:
Sprout Social is built for teams that manage social media as a function, not a side task. A calendar plans and schedules content across networks such as Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, X, and TikTok, and approval flows keep drafts under review before they go out. A smart inbox gathers messages, comments, and mentions from every channel into one stream that can be assigned, tagged, and replied to by a team.

Analytics are a major selling point. Reports show how posts perform, how audiences grow, and how competitors compare, and they can be exported or shared with clients and executives. Listening tools track brand mentions, topics, and sentiment across social and the web, which helps with crisis monitoring and market research. Influencer marketing and employee advocacy tools extend into related work. AI Assist helps write posts, change tone, and draft replies, and it can summarize sentiment from conversations.

item.title: Iconosquare
item.description:
Iconosquare started as an Instagram analytics tool and expanded to other networks. Social teams connect accounts and see how posts perform, when audiences are active, and how growth compares with competitors. Reports can be exported for clients, which makes it popular with agencies.

Scheduling and planning tools let teams build a content calendar and publish across networks. AI features suggest captions and hashtags, and a listening module monitors mentions and comments. The focus is on analysis that guides what to post, more than on broad community management.

item.title: Latte Social
item.description:
Latte Social covers the basics of content planning. Users connect accounts, ask the AI for post ideas and captions tuned to a brand’s voice, schedule content on a calendar, and publish to several networks. The tool aims to keep a steady posting schedule without constant effort.

For small teams and individual creators, that combination of drafting and scheduling reduces time spent on routine social tasks. AI-generated posts are a starting point and tend to be generic without personal details and specific examples.

item.title: Loomly
item.description:
Loomly supports the planning side of social media. Teams build a content calendar, get post ideas from trends and prompts, draft posts with images and links, and route them through an approval workflow before publishing. A brand asset library keeps logos and images handy.

The platform previews how a post will look on each network and schedules publishing. Analytics show performance, and ad management features support boosted posts. AI assists with captions and ideas.

item.title: Pallyy
item.description:
Pallyy keeps social management simple and affordable. Users connect accounts, plan posts on a visual calendar, and publish to several networks. A first-comment feature, link-in-bio pages, and a media library support common creator workflows, and a unified inbox collects comments and messages.

Analytics show growth and engagement, and client-friendly reports help agencies prove results. Collaboration tools let clients approve content before it goes live. AI features suggest captions, hashtags, and ideas to speed up planning.

item.title: Publer
item.description:
Publer provides the essentials of social media planning at a modest price. Users connect accounts, build a calendar, schedule posts and recurring content, and see analytics on performance. Bulk scheduling and a library of media help manage volume.

Features include collaboration and approvals, link in bio pages, and a social inbox. The AI assistant writes captions, suggests hashtags, and repurposes content, and tools recycle evergreen posts.

Publer has a free plan with limits and paid tiers by social accounts. Alternatives include Buffer, Later, Metricool, Hootsuite, and Pallyy. Publer suits creators and small teams who want an affordable scheduler.

item.title: Vista Social
item.description:
Vista Social covers social publishing end to end. Teams connect profiles, plan a calendar, schedule content, and respond to comments and messages in one inbox. Approval workflows suit agencies working with clients, and reports summarize performance.

The platform includes reputation management, with review monitoring, and tools for tracking competitors. The AI assistant writes captions, suggests hashtags, and repurposes content. It supports newer networks quickly, which agencies value.

Vista Social has a free plan and paid tiers by profiles and users. Alternatives include Hootsuite, Sprout Social, Buffer, Later, and Agorapulse. Vista Social suits agencies and brands managing many accounts.

item.title: Pounce
item.description:
Pounce helps with timely engagement. It monitors social platforms for topics and conversations related to a brand or niche, flags those gaining traction, and suggests ways to participate, such as posting a response or creating content.

Social media managers use it to catch trends early, when joining a conversation can earn reach. Faster detection and suggested angles shorten the path from trend to post.

Independent information is limited. Brands should be careful about jumping on trends, as tone-deaf posts cause harm. Pounce has a free tier and paid plans. Alternatives include Brandwatch, Sprout Social listening, Exploding Topics, BuzzSumo, and Google Trends. Pounce suits social managers who want trend alerts.

item.title: Predis.ai
item.description: Predis.ai aims to make social content creation quick for small businesses and creators. You enter a prompt or paste a link to your product page or website, choose a format such as a single image, carousel, or short video, and the tool generates a post with a caption, hashtags, and a branded design. Editing tools let you change the text, images, and layout, and apply your brand colors and logo.

item.title: Taplio
item.description:
Taplio focuses on LinkedIn, where personal branding and B2B outreach happen. Users can generate post ideas and drafts in their own voice, find high-performing posts for inspiration, schedule content, and use carousels and templates. The AI learns from successful posts and tries to match your tone, saving time for busy founders, consultants, and sales professionals.

It includes tools beyond writing. Analytics show which posts and topics resonate and how followers grow, an engagement feature suggests relevant posts to comment on, and a lead database helps find and track potential customers. Team plans allow agencies and ghostwriters to manage multiple accounts.

item.title: Typefully
item.description:
Typefully started as a better way to write threads on X. The editor is clean and focused, with automatic thread splitting, a preview of how the post will look, and collaboration so someone else can review drafts. Posts can be scheduled, queued, and cross-posted to several networks, so one piece of writing can reach audiences on different platforms.

Analytics and growth features help creators learn what works. Dashboards show impressions, engagement, and follower trends, and tools help plan content, track ideas, and reuse past posts. AI features suggest rewrites, hooks, and alternatives, and can adjust tone, though the tool emphasizes the writer’s voice.
